CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: China should continue engaging in negotiations with the US while maintaining a firm stance on core interests. We should avoid further escalation that could trigger additional US tariffs on the remaining ~$300 billion of Chinese goods, while not making unilateral concessions that undermine our industrial policy goals. A negotiated partial deal that secures tariff rollback on existing duties in exchange for increased agricultural purchases is the best available outcome.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is significant but not existential at this stage. UNCTAD data shows US tariffs caused a $35 billion export loss for China in H1 2019, with office machinery and communication equipment hit hardest (55% decline). However, Chinese firms maintained 75% of their tariffed exports to the US, demonstrating resilience. The yuan depreciated over 5% against the dollar in 2018, providing a partial offset. The real danger is further escalation: Trump has threatened tariffs on all remaining Chinese imports (~$300 billion), which would devastate consumer electronics and broader export sectors. The IMF has already cut global growth forecasts citing trade tensions. China's strategic retaliation on $110 billion of US goods, targeting Republican-district products like soybeans, has provided some leverage but cannot offset the asymmetry of US tariff reach. The Phase One deal discussions offer a path to freeze escalation and roll back some existing tariffs in exchange for agricultural purchases—a manageable concession that preserves space for China's long-term tech self-sufficiency goals under Made in China 2025.
key_factors: US tariffs caused $35 billion Chinese export loss in H1 2019 (UNCTAD)
Trump threatened tariffs on remaining ~$300 billion of Chinese imports
Office machinery and communication equipment sectors hit hardest with 55% trade decline
Chinese firms maintained 75% of tariffed exports showing resilience
Yuan depreciated 5%+ in 2018 providing partial offset
IMF cut global growth forecasts citing US-China trade tensions
Phase One deal negotiations ongoing as of decision date
Trade diversion to Vietnam, Mexico, Taiwan reducing China's market share

Chinese firms which, despite the substantial tariffs, maintained 75% of their exports to the US

The office machinery and communication equipment sectors were hit the hardest, suffering a $15 billion reduction of US imports from China as trade in tariffed goods in those sectors fell by an average of 55%
Trump has threatened additional tariffs of $267 billion worth of goods, meaning all Chinese imports could be subject to tariffs
The yuan fell over 5% against the US dollar last year, before broadly stabilising in 2019
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said the escalation of US-China trade tension was one factor to have contributed to a significantly weakened global expansion
Lighthizer and Mnuchin thought China was willing to rewrite key national security and trade laws to reduce the theft of intellectual property, open its markets to U.S. financial firms
